goal: flywheel.toml supports an optional [agent] table whose model key parses into WorkPolicy.model as a validated non-empty string, with the init scaffold documenting it as a commented example.

references: packages/flywheel-orchestrator/src/flywheel_orchestrator/_policy.py [paths] handling -- mirror the optional-table parse-and-validate pattern for [agent]
_INIT_POLICY in packages/flywheel-orchestrator/src/flywheel_orchestrator/_workflow.py -- the commented [[defaults.graders]] block is the model for the commented [agent] example
constraints: WorkPolicy.model defaults to None so every existing WorkPolicy construction and test stays valid unchanged
A file without [agent], or with [agent] but no model key, yields model=None
agent.model that is not a string, or is empty/whitespace-only, raises PolicyError whose message names the file and the agent.model key, matching existing PolicyError message style
[agent] present but not a table raises PolicyError matching the existing '[paths] must be a table' style
No allowlist of model ids; the value is an opaque string passed through verbatim
Update the policy format docstring at the top of _policy.py to document the [agent] table
The scaffolded flywheel.toml must still parse cleanly via load_policy after adding the commented [agent] example
Add test coverage for: absent table, valid model string, non-string model, empty-string model, non-table [agent], and the scaffold round-trip
Commit with a Conventional Commits message before emitting intent=verify
non_goals: No CLI flag or worker plumbing; that is the follow-up task worker-model-resolution
No changes to rubric judge_model, HarnessConfig.rubric_judge_model, or summarizer_model
No per-task model field on the core Task schema
edge_cases: Unknown keys under [agent] follow the existing policy posture for unknown keys (ignored); do not add new strictness
